Class MollweideProjection

java.lang.Object
edu.cnu.mdi.mapping.projection.MollweideProjection
All Implemented Interfaces:
IMapProjection
public class MollweideProjection extends Object implements IMapProjection
Mollweide equal-area pseudocylindrical projection (spherical Earth, R = 1).

Forward equations (Snyder)

Solve for the auxiliary angle θ using Newton-Raphson iteration:

  2θ + sin(2θ) = π sin φ

  x = (2√2 / π) · (λ - λ₀) · cos θ
  y = √2 · sin θ

Inverse equations

  θ = arcsin(y / √2)
  φ = arcsin((2θ + sin 2θ) / π)
  λ = λ₀ + π · x / (2√2 · cos θ)

Domain

The entire globe maps to an ellipse with semi-axes A = 2√2 (x) and B = √2 (y). Latitude is clamped to ±89.999° for numerical safety.

Seam handling

Like Mercator, the Mollweide projection has a seam at λ₀ ± π. crossesSeam(double, double) is overridden to detect polygon edges that straddle the seam so they can be split before rendering.

Default central meridian

The central longitude λ₀ defaults to -70° (western Atlantic). This choice is intentional: it positions the Americas near the centre for an aesthetically balanced view when the control panel occupies the right side of the window. It can be changed via setCentralLongitude(double).

    • crossesSeam

      public boolean crossesSeam(double lon1, double lon2)
      Tests whether the segment between two longitudes crosses the projection seam (the anti-meridian relative to the central longitude).

      Global cylindrical projections such as MercatorProjection and MollweideProjection override this method to detect wrap-around so that polygon edges that cross the seam can be split rather than drawn as a horizontal streak across the map.

      The default implementation returns false, which is correct for hemispherical projections (OrthographicProjection, LambertEqualAreaProjection) where no seam split is needed.

      Returns true when the two longitudes — each wrapped relative to λ₀ — differ by more than π radians, indicating an antimeridian crossing.

      Specified by:
      crossesSeam in interface IMapProjection
      Parameters:
      lon1 - first longitude in radians
      lon2 - second longitude in radians
      Returns:
      true if the segment crosses the seam; false otherwise

    • isLongitudePeriodic

      public boolean isLongitudePeriodic()
      Reports whether the projection's horizontal domain represents a complete, periodically wrapped 360-degree longitude range.

      Adaptive graticule rendering uses this distinction when the entire projected width is visible. Sampling the two horizontal edges of such a projection produces the same seam longitude and can otherwise make half the world appear to be outside the visible longitude extent.

      Specified by:
      isLongitudePeriodic in interface IMapProjection
      Returns:
      true for full-width periodic projections such as Mercator and Mollweide; otherwise false

    • latLonToXY

      public void latLonToXY(Point2D.Double latLon, Point2D.Double xy)
      Forward projection: geographic (λ, φ) → projection-space (x, y).

      Implementations should clamp the latitude to their valid range before computing to avoid NaN or Infinity results at the poles.

      For hemispherical projections (e.g. orthographic) a point on the far side of the globe should set xy to (Double.NaN, Double.NaN) rather than throwing, because callers test isPointVisible separately.

      Latitude is clamped to [MIN_LAT, MAX_LAT] before solving for θ. The relative longitude (λ - λ₀) is wrapped to [-π, π) to handle inputs that span the seam.

      Specified by:
      latLonToXY in interface IMapProjection
      Parameters:
      latLon - input geographic point in radians (x=λ, y=φ); must not be null
      xy - output projection-space point; must not be null

    • isPointVisible

      public boolean isPointVisible(Point2D.Double latLon)
      Tests whether a geographic location is visible in this projection.

      Global projections (Mercator, Mollweide, Lambert) generally return true for any point within their latitude range. Hemispherical projections (Orthographic) return true only for points on the visible hemisphere.

      The entire globe maps to the Mollweide ellipse, so every point within the latitude range is visible.

      Specified by:
      isPointVisible in interface IMapProjection
      Parameters:
      latLon - geographic point in radians (x=λ, y=φ)
      Returns:
      true if the point is visible; false otherwise

    • isPointOnMap

      public boolean isPointOnMap(Point2D.Double xy)
      Tests whether a projection-space point lies within the valid domain of this projection.

      This is used after IMapProjection.latLonToXY(Point2D.Double, Point2D.Double) to guard against rendering points that fall slightly outside the projection boundary due to floating-point rounding.

      A point is on the map when it lies within or on the boundary of the Mollweide ellipse: x²/A² + y²/B² ≤ 1.

      Specified by:
      isPointOnMap in interface IMapProjection
      Parameters:
      xy - projection-space point
      Returns:
      true if the point is on (or inside) the map; false otherwise

    • drawMapOutline

      public void drawMapOutline(Graphics2D g2, IContainer container)
      Draws the outer boundary of the projection domain.

      Typical implementations build a Path2D in world coordinates, transform each vertex to screen space via container.worldToLocal, then stroke the path using colors and widths from the current MapTheme.

      Draws the Mollweide ellipse boundary (x²/A² + y²/B² = 1) using the theme's outline color and stroke width.

      Specified by:
      drawMapOutline in interface IMapProjection
      Parameters:
      g2 - graphics context to draw into
      container - container providing the world-to-local transform

    • drawLatitudeLine

      public void drawLatitudeLine(Graphics2D g2, IContainer container, double latitude)
      Draws a line of constant latitude (a parallel) at the given latitude.

      Implementations should approximate the curve by sampling at a sufficient number of longitude values, projecting each sample, and connecting the resulting screen points with a polyline. The line color must be MapTheme.getGraticuleColor() so that theme switching takes full effect.

      Draws a horizontal line across the map at the given latitude. The line is clipped to the Mollweide ellipse boundary, so it may be shorter than the full width of the map if the latitude is near the poles. Uses MapTheme.getGraticuleColor() so the color respects theme switching.
      Specified by:
      drawLatitudeLine in interface IMapProjection
      Parameters:
      g2 - graphics context
      container - container providing the world-to-local transform
      latitude - latitude φ in radians, typically in [-π/2, π/2]

    • drawLongitudeLine

      public void drawLongitudeLine(Graphics2D g2, IContainer container, double longitude)
      Draws a line of constant longitude (a meridian) at the given longitude.

      Implementations should approximate the curve by sampling at a sufficient number of latitude values, projecting each sample, and connecting the resulting screen points with a polyline. The line color must be MapTheme.getGraticuleColor() so that theme switching takes full effect.

      Samples 360 evenly spaced latitudes at the given longitude and connects the projected screen points. Uses MapTheme.getGraticuleColor() so the color respects theme switching.

      Specified by:
      drawLongitudeLine in interface IMapProjection
      Parameters:
      g2 - graphics context
      container - container providing the world-to-local transform
      longitude - longitude λ in radians, typically in [-π, π]

    • getProjection

      public EProjection getProjection()
      Returns the EProjection enum constant that identifies this implementation, if this projection is one of MDI's built-in projections.

      Application-supplied projections are allowed to return null. This permits an application to provide a projection without modifying EProjection, ProjectionFactory, or other MDI built-in projection registries.

      Specified by:
      getProjection in interface IMapProjection
      Returns:
      the built-in projection type, or null for a custom application-supplied projection

    • getXYBounds

      public Rectangle2D.Double getXYBounds()
      Returns the bounding rectangle of the projection-space domain in world coordinates.

      This rectangle is used by IContainer implementations to build the initial world-to-screen transform. The returned rectangle should tightly enclose the entire valid projected domain (e.g. [-π, π] × [MIN_Y, MAX_Y] for Mercator).

      Returns the bounding rectangle of the Mollweide ellipse: [-A, -B] to [A, B], i.e. [-2√2, -√2] to [2√2, √2].

      Specified by:
      getXYBounds in interface IMapProjection
      Returns:
      bounding rectangle in projection space; never null

    • createClipShape

      public Shape createClipShape(IContainer container)
      Creates a clip Shape in device coordinates that matches the projection's valid domain.

      This shape is used to:

      • Clip land/ocean rendering to the map region.
      • Fill the ocean background via IMapProjection.fillOcean(Graphics2D, IContainer).

      Returns an elliptical path in device coordinates that matches the Mollweide boundary, used as a clip region for ocean fill and land rendering.

      Specified by:
      createClipShape in interface IMapProjection
      Parameters:
      container - container providing the world-to-local transform
      Returns:
      a device-space Shape, or null if no clip is defined for this projection
